transcript.text: Good morning everyone. Let's get the pre-overtime huddle started for the weekend production of 480 pump housings in Assembly Cell 8. We have the standard weekend plan — one Saturday shift and one Sunday shift, up to 8 hours each, with two operators per shift. Before I approve the final weekend plan, I need to hear from workforce coordination, maintenance, and quality on any constraints. Who'd like to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Nora. I'll go first from workforce coordination. I need to flag a certification constraint for Cell 8 this weekend. After the last training audit, I checked the updated certification matrix, and it specifies required rosters for both days. Saturday's Cell 8 shift must be staffed with Lina, who is setup-certified, and Sam, who is run-certified. Sunday's shift must be Ruth, who is setup-certified, and Omar, who is run-certified. The updated roster hasn't been attached to the weekend work order yet, so I want to make sure everyone is aware before we lock the plan.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a maintenance constraint for Cell 8 this weekend. During my morning walkaround inspection, I found that Cell 8's conveyor servo requires a 90-minute preventive inspection between the Saturday and Sunday shifts. I recorded this finding in my maintenance notebook, but I haven't entered it in the electronic work order yet. We need to account for this 90-minute window between shifts so the servo inspection can be completed before Sunday production starts.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a quality constraint for Cell 8 this weekend. The customer quality amendment requires 12 first-off units after the weekend setup, and 100% torque verification on the first 30 units after the maintenance restart, with quality signoff before the remaining units are released. I received the signed amendment by email, but it has not yet been linked to the order record. This means we need to account for the time to produce and inspect those 12 first-off units after Saturday setup, and then after Sunday's maintenance restart, we need time to produce and torque-verify the first 30 units before the rest can proceed.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Attach the updated certification roster to the weekend work order.
Enter the 90-minute conveyor servo preventive inspection into the electronic work order.
Link the signed customer quality amendment to the order record.
Ensure the 90-minute servo inspection is scheduled between Saturday and Sunday shifts, before Sunday production starts.
Quality must sign off on the 12 first-off units after Saturday setup and on the 100% torque verification of the first 30 units after Sunday maintenance restart before remaining units are released.
